slides.say: A B C D is an isosceles trapezoid, with A D parallel to B C. Given: A B and A D are seven centimeters, and angle A B D is thirty degrees. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
at: A B C D is an isosceles trapezoid

slides.say: The perimeter is the sum of the four sides. Three of them are given, A B, A D, and C D, which equals A B because the trapezoid is isosceles. [short pause] We need the fourth side, B C.
[short pause] Start with the first given. A B equals A D, so triangle A B D is isosceles. In an isosceles triangle the base angles are equal. Angle A B D is thirty, so angle A D B is thirty too.
at: so triangle A B D is isosceles

slides.say: Thirty and thirty. So the top angle, A, is one hundred eighty minus sixty, which is one hundred twenty.

In every trapezoid, the two angles on the same leg add up to one hundred eighty. A is one hundred twenty, so all of angle B is sixty. Its lower part, angle D B C, is sixty minus thirty, which is thirty.
at: so all of angle B is sixty

slides.say: Another way to see the thirty is our familiar Z. The bases are parallel, so the two angles in the corners of the Z are equal. Thirty and thirty.
The trapezoid is isosceles, so the two angles on the bottom base are equal. Angle C equals angle B, sixty. You can also see it because angle C completes angle A to one hundred eighty.

What did we get? Triangle B C D has thirty and sixty, together ninety. So the angle at D completes it to one hundred eighty, and it's ninety. It's not just a right triangle. It's a gold triangle, thirty, sixty, ninety.
at: Triangle B C D has thirty and sixty

slides.say: Its short leg is the one across from the thirty, C D. The trapezoid is isosceles, so C D equals A B, seven.
at: so C D equals A B

slides.say: When we know the short leg, the hypotenuse is easy. It's exactly twice the short leg. So B C is fourteen.
The perimeter is seven plus seven plus seven plus fourteen, which is thirty-five. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: One more link. Triangle A B D has angles thirty, thirty and one hundred twenty, the triangle we met with the special triangles. So B D is seven root three. That matches the gold triangle, where the long leg is the short leg times root three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: So B D is seven root three
